description: Bridge with ball squeeze guide: a glute bridge with a ball between the knees for glutes, inner thighs and pelvic floor, plus mistakes and variations.
intro: This bridge adds a ball or pillow between your knees, so your inner thighs work while your glutes lift your hips. The inner thigh muscles attach close to the pelvic floor, and many women find a gentle pelvic-floor lift easier to feel when the thighs press together.
feel: You should feel your buttocks working, your inner thighs pressing the ball and a light lift inside the pelvis as you rise. After the two-second hold, lower and let everything relax. Your breath keeps moving and your lower back stays neutral. Bearing down, breath holding or neck strain mean you should squeeze less.

mistakes.wrong: Crushing the ball as hard as you can
mistakes.right: Use a steady, moderate squeeze. A maximal grip spreads to the belly and makes you hold your breath.

mistakes.wrong: Letting the ball slip as you lift
mistakes.right: Keep the pressure even from the start of the lift to the end of the lowering.
Release the ball, glutes and pelvic floor completely before the next rep.

easier: Squeeze the ball without lifting your hips, or lift only a few inches.
harder: Hold the top longer, lower more slowly, or add a gentle Kegel on the lift and full relaxation on the way down.
who: Women who want more support around the pelvis, including those over 40 or working on bladder control, and anyone who struggles to feel the pelvic floor in a plain bridge.
skip: Skip or modify with pelvic pain, groin or inner thigh pain, or a pelvic floor that feels tight, since extra squeezing may not help. After recent surgery, a recent birth or in later pregnancy, check with your doctor or pelvic floor physiotherapist first. Stop if it hurts.

faq.q: Why squeeze a ball during a bridge?
faq.a: It works the inner thighs along with the glutes, and many people feel the pelvic floor more easily that way. It adds support but does not replace Kegels.

faq.q: What size ball should I use?
faq.a: A soft ball about the size of a small playground ball works well. A firm pillow or rolled towel is just as good.
